idea.description: SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over a user's interaction history. Item and positional embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting representation scores candidate items by dot product. Attention can emphasize recent interactions or longer-range dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
idea.motivation: Combine the simplicity useful for sparse histories with the ability to capture longer sequential patterns. SASRec is an established starting baseline; the supplied description does not specify a new cold-start mechanism. Learned item embeddings alone cannot reliably represent items without training interactions.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and preserve all four dataset routes. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts within the trial directory. Select using macro validation HR@10 under the pinned evaluator. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), including measured metrics and definitions. Architecture changes require matching predictor-writer and diagnostic adaptations. No experiments or performance measurements were performed for this summary.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the prescribed training and validation splits.
  Initialize SASRec with training seed 42.
  For each training batch:
    Encode padded histories with causal attention.
    Score next-item positives and sampled negatives.
    Minimize binary cross-entropy over non-padding positions.
  Save model artifacts and compatible predictor code.
Compare trials using host-reported macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Provides a well-defined sequential recommendation baseline.
originality.negative: SASRec is established; no novel cold-start extension is described. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Public titles and descriptions could support a separately evaluated content-aware extension for sparse items.
future_potential.negative: Any improvement remains hypothetical until validated within the shared search budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The prescribed baseline already supplies the central model and dataset routing.
code_difficulty.negative: Changes must keep training, generated prediction code, and diagnostic interfaces consistent.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
